'''''Eucomis comosa''''', the '''pineapple flower''', '''pineapple lily''' or '''wine eucomis''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the asparagus [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asparagaceae]] (subfamily [[Scilloideae]]). A [[deciduous]] [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] used as an [[ornamental plant]], it is [[endemic]] to [[South Africa]]. The white to purple flowers appear in summer and are arranged in a spike ([[raceme]]), topped by a "head" of green leaflike bracts.

==Description==
''Eucomis comosa'' is a [[perennial plant]], growing from a large [[bulb]], which is often purple in colour. The leaves form a basal rosette, and are {{cvt|30|–|80|cm|in|0}} long by {{cvt|3|–|10|cm|in|frac=2}} wide, with a smooth, slightly undulating margin. The leaves usually have purple spots and may have an overall purple tinge; var. ''striata'' has purple stripes. The [[inflorescence]], a [[raceme]], appears in summer (late July or early August in the UK) and is borne on a stem ([[Peduncle (botany)|peduncule]]) {{cvt|40|–|60|cm|in|0}} tall. Individual flowers have stalks ([[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]) {{cvt|15|–|20|mm|in|frac=16}} long. The [[tepal]]s are whitish to purple, the ovary always purple. Most plants have a pleasant coconut-like scent. The inflorescence is topped by a head (coma) of bracts, often purple spotted or tinged like the leaves.<ref name=Comp90/> The overall effect is of a miniature pineapple plant (''Ananas comosus''), though in fact the two species are not closely related.<ref name=RHSPF/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Martinus Houttuyn|Maarten Houttuyn]] in 1780, as ''Asphodelus comosus''.<ref name=WCSP_305891/> The specific epithet ''comosus'' (shared by the [[pineapple]], ''Ananas comosus'') means "tufted".<ref name=RHSLG/> In 1929, {{ill|Heinrich Rudolf Wehrhahn|es}} transferred the species to ''[[Eucomis]]''.<ref name=WCSP_305891/> It is one of a group of larger [[tetraploid]] species of ''[[Eucomis]]'', with 2''n'' = 4''x'' = 60.<ref name=ZonnDunc10/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Eucomis comosa'' is native to the east [[Cape Provinces]] and the province of [[KwaZulu-Natal]] in South Africa.<ref name=WCSP_305891/> It is found in rocky ground at elevations of around {{cvt|1600|m|ft}}.<ref name=Comp90/>

==Cultivation==
''Eucomis comosa'' is an ornamental plant with numerous [[cultivar]]s, varying in colour from forms with white flowers and little or no purple on the leaves, to forms with deeply coloured leaves. Described as "surprisingly hardy" in the UK,<ref name=Comp90/> down to {{cvt|-5|or|-10|C|F}},<ref name=Comp90/><ref name=RHSPF/> it needs a sheltered spot in full sun, and a protective mulch in winter when grown where frosts occur.<ref name=RHSPF/> In the UK, the compact [[cultivar]] 'Leia' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/367947/eucomis-comosa-leia/details | title = ''Eucomis comosa'' 'Leia' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 8 September 2023}}</ref>
